Ký hiệu: MQ/2026E_ Số: 0004417 Ngày 14 tháng 03 năm 2026 Đơn vị bán hàng: CÔNG T

classification: COMPOUND: two distinct facts, both verified directly from the IR. (1) production's own compute_reading_order output for this page is itself non-monotonic in y -- element e7 ('San pham A-100', y0=596.5, a table-like data cell) is placed BEFORE e6 ('Mo ta hang hoa', y0=547.6, the header cell immediately above it) in Page.reading_order. This is a genuine defect in compute_reading_order's column-banding heuristic when applied to the scattered small text fragments a shattered/undetected table produces (the same picture-label table-gating failure documented in 025's causal chain for sibling documents cmb_stamp_table_vi / hc_stamp_table_vi). (2) Layer 1's document_text (and 027's canonical-table counterfactual, which only reorders TABLE cells) both iterate page.elements in raw creation-order, NEVER consulting Page.reading_order or order_index at all. For THIS document raw creation order happens to place e6 before e7 (168 < 183), so order_ok reads True by coincidence, while page_order_ok -- which is the first Layer-2 or Layer-1 metric to actually read Page.reading_order -- correctly reports False. FORMAL RESULT: Layer 1 cannot distinguish 'the element list was appended in an order that happens to look right' from 'the computed reading order is right' -- it never inspects the field production computes for this exact purpose. 025's claim that compute_reading_order is exonerated on SCAN-49 (0 order failures after canonical table serialization) was itself measured through this same blind raw-list channel and did not detect this case; page_order_ok is the first metric in the whole 023-029 lineage to read reading_order directly.

formal_counterexample.statement: Let e_a, e_b be two elements on the same page with true reading positions y0(e_a) < y0(e_b) (e_a is visually above e_b). Layer 1's document_text serializes elements in `page.elements` LIST order, which is creation/detection order and is NOT required to equal either geometric y-order or Page.reading_order. If list order happens to place e_a before e_b, Layer 1 scores any required strings in e_a, e_b as correctly ordered -- REGARDLESS of what Page.reading_order (production's own computed answer to 'what order does this page read in') says. Concretely: reading_order = [..., e7, e6, ...] (e7 before e6) while list order and Layer 1's serialization = [..., e6, e7, ...] (e6 before e7). Layer 1 reports order_ok=True; the field production computes specifically to answer this question says the opposite.
formal_counterexample.concrete_evidence: e6 'Mo ta hang hoa' y0=547.6, e7 'San pham A-100' y0=596.5. list/Layer1 order: e6,e7 (matches y0, coincidentally). Page.reading_order: e7,e6 (inverts y0 -- itself the defect). Layer1 order_ok reads list order (e6,e7) -> True. page_order_ok reads Page.reading_order (e7,e6) -> False.
